lede: A Rebel sector with **one extra beacon**, and that beacon is a second Flagship sitting half-built in its own shipyard. Killing the unfinished hull pays a weapon, 5 fuel, 5 missiles, 5 drone parts, **two jumps of breathing room** and a ship unlock, for a fight against 10 hull, shields running at 2 power of a possible 8, and no weapons at all. Everything else is the ordinary Rebel pool: six to eight beacons that open shooting, one guaranteed boarding, and seven events that can put the fleet a jump closer.
callout: **Versus a plain Rebel Controlled Sector: one row.** The same nine lists, the same minimums and maximums, the same start beacon — `FLAGSHIP_CONSTRUCTION` at 1–1 is the whole difference, and it is what makes this sector `unique` and keeps it out of the early game. The nebula line is the reason the spread looks so wide, and it is also the line that decides how much room the rest of the table gets: it is drawn before any of them, and it can come out at nothing or at a fifth of the map.

section_notes.FLAGSHIP_CONSTRUCTION: The one look at the Flagship before the Federation base, and the sector never starves it — it is the first line filled off the table, ahead of the fights, the stores and the fillers. Arriving costs nothing: the decline branch has no effects at all, so the beacon is a free look and a decision. What it will not survive is the fleet reaching it first, which rewrites whatever event was on a beacon.
section_notes.HOSTILE_REBEL: Five events, every one of them shooting the moment you arrive. Two are scouts that will run — and if {{AUTO_WARNING}} or {{SQUAT_WARNING}} gets its FTL charged and jumps out, Rebel pursuit doubles for a jump. Killing them is worth a low-to-medium reward; letting them go costs you the map.
section_notes.BOARDERS_REBEL: Fixed at one beacon, so a boarding is guaranteed somewhere in the sector. It resolves as either {{BOARDERS_SUN}} — 2–4 humans aboard, alongside a star, with no choice offered at all — or {{BOARDERS_REBEL_SHIP}}, which puts 2–3 aboard while a Rebel ship shoots at you.
section_notes.NEUTRAL_REBEL: The line the map runs out on, and losing it costs more than its size suggests: this is the whole choose-your-fight half of the sector — three guarded stations, the transport, the derelict scout, the defector — plus the only fleet delay here outside the shipyard, at {{AUTO_DEFENSE_RADAR}}. Each of the three guarded stations has a way past the guard that does not involve the guard.
section_notes.NEBULA_REBEL: Eleven events for anywhere between none and five beacons, and they are all cloud stops: in a sector that is not itself a nebula, sitting in one **halves the fleet's advance** for that jump, which makes this the cheapest brake on the clock the sector has. The price is sensors down, three plasma storms running your reactor at half power, and {{NEBULA_REBEL_BOARDING}} — an ambush with no ship to shoot back at.
section_notes.DISTRESS_BEACON_REBEL: One or two beacons carrying six events, and every distress marker this sector can draw comes from this line — nothing in the other pools carries the tag, so unlike most sectors the markers on the map never outrun the table. Two of the three routes to the hidden Federation base sit here rather than in the quest entry: {{CIVILIAN_ASTEROIDS_BEACON}} and {{REBEL_VS_FEDERATION}}.
section_notes.ITEMS: Thirteen events for one or two beacons: refuelling, repairs, hiring, and trades in both directions. Nothing in it is dangerous and nothing in it is free.
section_notes.QUESTS_REBEL: Allocated 0–2, so a run through here can be handed no quest marker at all from this line. Where the marker lands is a second problem: a quest taken with few jumps left is pushed into the next sector instead, it can never be placed inside the cloud, and if this is your seventh sector the pushed quest is cancelled outright. {{MERCHANT_REQUEST}} at least pays 5 drone parts up front just for taking the job.

chain.title: The second Flagship · one beacon, guaranteed

steps.title: {{FLAGSHIP_CONSTRUCTION}}
steps.detail: Scaffolding, construction drones, and planets mined out to feed something enormous. **Leaving immediately costs nothing** — the decline branch has no effects at all, and this is the only look at the ship before the Federation base.

steps.title: Look around, and it powers up
steps.detail: The scan identifies a **second Flagship** under construction, and the fight starts with no further choice. It is built on the Flagship's own third-phase layout with almost none of the power in it: **10 hull**, shields at 2 power of a possible 8, and two artillery mounts running at 1 power of 4. The finished third phase has 20 hull, shields at 6 or 8, and both mounts at full.

steps.title: It has no weapons — it has a teleporter
steps.detail: The weapons block is commented out of the blueprint, so everything it fires is artillery. Three human crew, a teleporter and a `sabotage` boarding AI; hacking and mind control are installed but switched off at the start. Blowing the hull and killing the crew both reach the same salvage.

steps.title: Salvage, and a prototype sent home
steps.detail: A high weapon reward, 5 fuel, 5 missiles, 5 drone parts, and the Rebel fleet pushed back **two jumps**. On the way out you find the captured Federation cruiser they were reverse-engineering and program its FTL to fly itself home — which is the unlock.

items.text: The sector's best key: past the guard into the cache at {{AUTO_DEFENSE_ITEM}} and, graded across two levels, at {{NEBULA_AUTO_DEFENSE_ITEM}}; out of the storm fight at {{STORM_AUTO}}; and never seen at all at {{NEBULA_REBEL_UNDETECTED}}.

Beams onto the station at {{AUTO_DEFENSE_MAP}} for the map data with no fight, and takes the survivors straight off {{NEBULA_LOST_SHIP}} — a crew member and scrap with no roll at all. Also opens {{CIVILIAN_ASTEROIDS_BEACON}}, a combat-trained rescue at {{REBEL_VS_FEDERATION}}, and the way to pull your own people back out of {{MERCHANT_REQUEST}}.

Sensors 3 reads the station remotely at {{AUTO_DEFENSE_MAP}} and scans {{BROKEN_REBEL_DRONE}} before you wake it up — the plain download can turn a derelict scout into a live one. Sensors 2 or 3 and Long-Ranged Scanners each buy a second pass at the hidden Federation base, whichever event sent you there.

At {{AUTO_DEFENSE_RADAR}} one drone part buys the map and a jump of fleet delay outright, where the manual hack can just as easily trip the alarm and cost you one. Graded 1 and 2 into the cache at {{NEBULA_AUTO_DEFENSE_ITEM}}.

Engines 3 or 6 to outrun {{STORM_AUTO}}, Engines 4 to break contact once spotted at {{NEBULA_REBEL_UNDETECTED}}. Piloting 2 is the clean way through {{STORM_ITEMS}} — the gated outcomes contain no crew loss, no hull damage and no breach.

A Rockman or a repair drone walks into the fire at {{DISTRESS_STATION_FIRE}} — both skip the roll that kills someone, and pay an augment or a drone. Engi Med-bot Dispersal or a Healing Burst at {{REBEL_VS_FEDERATION}}; Adv. FTL Navigation at {{ESCORT_BEACON}}; a defence drone, repair drone or Rock Plating at {{CIVILIAN_ASTEROIDS_BEACON}}; any missile weapon at {{HELP_MINERS}}.
Not one named weapon, drone or augment drops anywhere in this pool, and the sector declares no store rarity list of its own — every item here is a random draw or a store shelf.

Twenty-three of the fifty events can end with someone new aboard, many of them through dead-crew salvage rather than a choice you make. {{TAVERN_HIRE}} is the only one that simply sells you one, and {{DISTRESS_STATION_FIRE}} is the only one that hands over a survivor with a name.

Three separate events plant the same marker — {{CIVILIAN_ASTEROIDS_BEACON}}, {{REBEL_VS_FEDERATION}} and {{FEDERATION_PLANET_SIGNAL}} — and one of the outcomes waiting there repairs **35 hull**. Sensors 2 or 3, or Long-Ranged Scanners, buy a second scan pass on top.

One store guaranteed, two at most, in a sector whose set-piece is a Flagship — this is a thin place to be counting on repairs. The item pool trades on top: {{NEBULA_TRADER}} and {{TRADER_CIV}} swap fuel, missiles and drone parts in both directions, {{SELL_MISSILES_STATION}} and {{SELL_DRONES_STATION}} turn ammunition back into scrap, and {{ESCORT_BEACON}} can finish with a shop on a distress beacon.

The most of anything this sector hands out. Besides the three Federation-base routes: {{MERCHANT_REQUEST}} (two different jobs), {{ESCORT_BEACON}}, and the defector's scrap cache at {{ALISON_DEFECTOR}}.
{{BROKEN_REBEL_DRONE}}, {{AUTO_DEFENSE_MAP}}, {{AUTO_DEFENSE_RADAR}} and {{REBEL_TRANSPORT}} can all reveal the sector map — useful here precisely because the shipyard beacon is worth routing to.

Seven events can double pursuit for a jump; only two can push it back, {{AUTO_DEFENSE_RADAR}} by one and the shipyard by two. Note what triggers it: scouts escaping at {{AUTO_WARNING}} and {{SQUAT_WARNING}}, losing your bearings at {{NEBULA_REBEL_UNDETECTED}}, and abandoning the family in the asteroid field at {{CIVILIAN_ASTEROIDS_BEACON}}.
Ten events in the pool start shooting on arrival, and the hostile entry alone is 6–8 beacons — the largest allocation on the page. Another eighteen events can end in combat if you push them.

Everything that boards you here is human. {{NEBULA_REBEL_BOARDING}} puts 3–4 aboard with the nebula blinding your sensors, {{BOARDERS_SUN}} 2–4 with solar flares landing on top, and neither offers a choice before it happens.

{{DISTRESS_STATION_FIRE}} and {{STORM_ITEMS}} can each kill someone outright, and both have a blue option that skips the risk entirely. The other two, {{ALISON_DEFECTOR}} and {{MERCHANT_REQUEST}}, both lose the crew member to someone you took aboard on purpose.

Six written outcomes once you take him aboard: three are the crew member you were promised, one gutted engines and a jump of pursuit, one two more boarders and a hole in the hull, one a dead crew member. Rejecting him is not free either — one of those outcomes leaves him loose on your ship as an intruder.

{{AUTO_DEFENSE_ITEM}}, {{AUTO_DEFENSE_MAP}} and {{AUTO_DEFENSE_RADAR}} all look optional and all turn hostile if the sneaky route rolls badly. Without the matching system the only ways in are a fight or a shrug.

items.lead: The shipyard hides in plain sight
items.text: Nothing labels it: no store icon, no distress icon, and Long-Ranged Scanners report no ship there. The one beacon worth planning a route around is the one the map refuses to point at, so plan the route from the sector's shape rather than from its markers.

A beacon the fleet takes is rewritten — the event that was waiting there and any hazard with it, replaced by an Elite Fighter that pays 1 fuel and no scrap, and outside the cloud by an anti-ship battery firing 3 damage and a breach. Everything in these pools is only on offer until the shading arrives, the shipyard included.

Sitting in a cloud halves the fleet's advance for that jump here, which is the only repeatable delay the sector sells — but sensors go dark inside, and a cloud beacon the fleet has already taken always comes with an ion storm on top.

A marker planted with few jumps left is pushed into the next sector rather than this one, it will not be placed inside the cloud, and if this sector is your seventh the pushed quest is cancelled instead — no sector 8 quests. Take the quest events early or treat them as pure combat encounters.

Only two things in this pool bring a hazard the cloud did not: the asteroid field at {{AUTO_ASTEROID}} and the red giant at {{BOARDERS_SUN}} — one a forced fight, one a forced boarding, and both readable one jump ahead with Long-Ranged Scanners.
